what: M3's "unopened preflop" is read as "preflop": every preflop spot takes the vpip branch, and no preflop spot falls through to the foldToRaise bar that M3's second clause ("facing a bet or raise before the river") would otherwise also cover.
why: The View the engine produces is {handle, cards, board, street, pot, toCall, stack, playersIn, position, legal} - no blind size and no raise count, and the blinds make the two spots arithmetically identical from inside it (unopened, pot = SB+BB and toCall = BB, two thirds of the pot; facing a 3x open, pot = SB+BB+open and toCall = open, two thirds again). legal.check does not separate them either. M3's own legs force this reading: Js Td is band 2 preflop, so tight-aggressive (leg f, folds) and loose-aggressive (leg g, raises to minRaiseTo) both come out "call" under the foldToRaise branch. The comment at decide() says what to split if a raise count is ever added to the View.

what: Spec rule 5's all-in clause is implemented as a raise-sizing rule (monster raises to maxRaiseTo; strong does when allInRate > ALL_IN_STRONG or when the all-in costs under CHEAP_CALL_SHARE of the stack beyond the call; everything else raises to minRaiseTo), and preflop raises always go to minRaiseTo.
why: M3 is the graded clause and it makes the fold bars absolute and names minRaiseTo as the preflop raise size, so rule 5 cannot be given any power to turn a fold into a call (that would break legs d and f, whose fixtures likely have a cheap call relative to the stack) nor to change the preflop size (leg g asserts minRaiseTo). Sizing is the one place rule 5's two constants, ALL_IN_STRONG and CHEAP_CALL_SHARE, can do real work without contradicting M3.
